title: What If You Were the Last Liar on Earth?

lines.text: At 3 a.m., you became the last liar on Earth.
By lunch, you've won 2,000 dollars at poker.
But nobody warns you what one lie at a party will cost.
Over the next 6 weeks, you'll make a million dollars. And you'll almost lose the one person who matters.
You don't know yet. You just want coffee.
Morning! Honestly, the coffee's burnt today. I burnt it.
Also, I don't like your jacket.
On the TV behind her, the weatherman looks like he hasn't slept.
Will it rain tomorrow? I have no idea. Nobody does. We guess.
You laugh, and say the first dumb thing that comes to mind.
I'm the manager. This one's on the house.
Oh! Sorry! On the house.
She believes you. Instantly. Completely.
Here's the thing. You were never good at spotting liars. Nobody is.
In studies, people catch a lie about 54 percent of the time. Barely better than flipping a coin.
Overnight, everyone else lost the ability to say anything they believe is false.
And because lies don't exist anymore, nobody expects one. Whatever you say, they believe.
The average person tells one or two lies a day. Today, the entire planet's total is... you.
Dude. Everyone's being so weird. My mom said my comedy is "not funny, but brave."
This is Theo. Your best friend since third grade. He's wanted to be a stand-up comedian for ten years.
He is not good.
Be honest. Am I funny?
And for the first time, you realize you're the only person on Earth who can answer that however you want.
...I gotta go.
Then your boss calls.
Hi Dana. I'm sick today.
Oh no! Honestly, I was going to fire you today. Feel better!
You're not sick. You are, apparently, about to be fired. You have bigger plans.
You open an online poker game.
Bluffing is just lying with chips. And nobody else can do it.
When they have a good hand, they bet. When they don't, they fold. They might as well be playing with their cards face up.
You go all in with a seven and a two. The worst hand in poker.
He must have something. I fold.
By lunch, you're up two thousand dollars. By Thursday, you're in Las Vegas.
Fun fact: counting cards isn't illegal in Las Vegas. But casinos can still ban you for being too good.
You last six hours.
Sir. Honestly? You scare me. Please leave.
And the small stuff works too.
Officer, I'm late for my own wedding.
Congratulations! Go, go!
It's our honeymoon.
First class. On us.
I'm a food critic.
...Everything is free. Please be kind.
Poker made you 41,000 dollars. But you're about to make 10 times that without touching a single card.
Every deal has a secret number. The most the buyer will pay. The least the seller will take.
Nobody can hide theirs anymore.
Your car is dying, so you visit a dealership.
This one's twenty-four thousand. Honestly, my boss lets me go down to nineteen. And the brakes squeak.
Seventeen. Final offer. Another dealer's waiting for me.
There is no other dealer.
...Seventeen it is.
Psychologists have found that the first number on the table drags the final price toward it. They call it anchoring.
And you're now the only person on Earth who can drop a fake anchor.
So you start a business. Negotiator for hire. Salaries, houses, contracts. You take ten percent.
The budget for this job is ninety thousand. Honestly, we'd go to a hundred and ten.
My client already has an offer for a hundred and twenty.
Your client gets a hundred and fifteen. You get eleven thousand five hundred dollars. For one phone call.
Then you have the idea that makes you a millionaire in 6 weeks. And it almost costs you your best friend.
If nobody can lie, every famous person on Earth has a problem. Because someone can just... ask.
Episode one: a pop star.
Did you write your own songs?
...No. A man named Gary writes all of them. I've never met Gary.
Episode two: the boss of a snack company.
Is your new chip healthy?
It's mostly salt and regret.
Technically, they're allowed to stay silent. But on live TV, silence is an answer too.
Ten million views. Then forty million. Sponsors line up, and every one of them has to tell you exactly how much they're willing to pay.
Six weeks in, you're a millionaire.
Theo comes to watch a taping.
Be honest. Can I do the warm-up act?
You let him. It does not go well.
I'm not laughing because it's not funny.
Theo laughs it off. But you notice he stops carrying his joke notebook.
That night, you tell one lie as a joke. By 2 a.m., half the city is about to lose its money.
Someone at a party asks what you think about Harbor Bank. Half the city keeps their money there.
Harbor Bank? It's going under. Get your money out tonight.
Everyone at the party believes you. Of course they do.
Then they text their friends. Who also can't imagine anyone would lie.
And this part isn't fiction. In 2023, customers of a real bank, Silicon Valley Bank, tried to pull out 42 billion dollars in a single day. The next morning, regulators shut it down.
A bank doesn't have to be broken to fail. It just needs enough people to believe it is.
By 2 a.m., there's a line around the block. In the rain.
So you go live on your own show.
I made it up. It was a joke. Harbor Bank is fine.
That one's true. They believe that too. The line goes home.
But Theo was at that party. And Theo isn't stupid.
Wait. That was a lie. You can lie.
...Yeah.
Since when?
Since everyone else stopped.
So every time I asked if I was funny...
You never answered. Not once. And that was its own answer.
Here's what nobody tells you about a world without lies: you'd never hear "you look great" again. Not once. It's lonely.
A lot of everyday lies aren't selfish at all. They're told to protect someone else. "I love it." "You look great." "You were amazing up there."
All of that is gone. From everyone. Except you.
A week later, Theo calls.
I'm doing one last set. Open mic, Friday. After that, I'm done. For real.
A basement comedy club. Forty people. Theo walks out.
And he's... okay. Not great. But there's one joke, about his mom calling his comedy "brave," that gets a real laugh.
Forty honest people. One real laugh. That's not nothing.
After the show, he finds you by the door.
Be honest. Was it good?
You're the only person on Earth who gets to choose the answer.
You could tell him the truth. Three out of ten. One great joke.
Or you could say the one thing nobody else is allowed to say anymore.
It was the best set I've ever seen.
He knows you can lie. He looks at you for a long time.
Thanks. I needed someone to say it.
And he keeps going.
A year later, Theo has a real show. Two hundred seats. Most of them laugh.
At 3 a.m., your phone buzzes. It's Theo.
Remember the night you said I was amazing?
Yeah.
Honestly? I was terrible.
Honestly? You were.
You both laugh until four.
You still have the show. You still win poker night, every Thursday.
And you only lie when it's kind. Mostly.
So, if you were the last liar on Earth, what would you do first? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe.
